hints.title: Transitive Province Partition Obstacle
hints.text: Direct and indirect connections partition cities into disjoint groups. How can traversing adjacent city pairs connect isolated elements and maintain an ongoing count of distinct connected provinces?

hints.title: Equivalence Relation Component Invariant
hints.text: Direct connections establish an equivalence relation. Merging groups whenever an active connection spans two different representatives accurately tracks connected components.

hints.title: Matrix Pair Union Procedure
hints.text: Initialize n disjoint components. Iterate over all pairs (i, j) where j > i in the connectivity matrix. Whenever the matrix entry is 1, resolve the canonical representatives for cities i and j. If they differ, merge their components and decrement the total province count. Return the remaining province count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Iterating through the upper triangle of the N x N matrix checks N * (N - 1) / 2 pairs.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: DFS requires creating an explicit adjacency graph and maintaining boolean visited flags.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Parent array uses O(N) space without needing additional adjacency lists.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Iterating only the upper triangle j > i to avoid redundant union checks.
